note: Mohanty et al. 2016, Frontiers in Plant Science (peer-reviewed). 54,306 images, 38 classes, 14 crops; abstract says 99.35% held-out (results section says 99.34%). Internet sets: 121 images 31.40% (GoogLeNet segmented TL 80-20), 119 images 31.69% (GoogLeNet color TL 80-20).

PlantDoc (Singh et al., CoDS-COMAD 2020, peer-reviewed; arXiv 1911.10317). Table 1: VGG16 PVD->uncropped PlantDoc 15.08%. Table 2: ImageNet+PVD trained, tested on C-PD 19.73/30.78/39.87; ImageNet+PVD fine-tuned on C-PD 60.41/62.06/70.53. Note 'PlantVillage only' models still use ImageNet init; upper end is 70.5%, slightly above '60-70%'. Uncropped fine-tuned only reaches 29.73% (VGG16).

GitHub repo: CC-BY-4.0, 2,598 data points, 13 species, up to 17 disease classes (27 classes total incl. 10 healthy; train dir shows 28 folders). Paper: images collected 'by using scientific and common names of 38 classes mentioned in the dataset by Mohanty et al.' All listed train folders map to PlantVillage crop/disease classes (incl. bell pepper, blueberry, cherry, peach, raspberry, soybean, squash, strawberry). Listed folders match evidence.

PlantDoc paper quotes confirmed: 'some images in the dataset which can potentially be wrongly classified' (attributed to lack of domain expertise); Fig. 6 caption says Tomato bacterial leaf spot and Septoria 'looks similar and are hard to label using visual features alone'.

arXiv 2603.13354v3 (Apr 2026), preprint, no peer-reviewed venue. AgriPath-LF16: 111,307 images, 16 crops, 65 crop-disease pairs (41 diseases). Lab-only ResNet-50 96.7->4.3, ConvNeXt-Tiny 97.5->6.3; full training ResNet-50 97.2 lab vs 69.9 field; avg relative drop ~25.6% CNNs, ~20.2% generative VLMs (full training). Note: ResNet-50 single-model relative drop is ~28%; the 20-25% is an average.
